texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have been at odds for days, and at supper it came out: raised voices over the table, and a bowl pushed away. {HOLDER_nameDef} would like to sit the two of them down together before it goes any further.

[peacemaker] Supper went quiet when {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} started on each other again. {HOLDER_nameDef}, who keeps the peace in the colony, says this is exactly what that is for, and would sit them down tonight.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} quarrelled across the fire at the evening meal, loudly enough that the children went quiet. {HOLDER_nameDef} offers to sit with the two of them and have it out properly.

li.label: {HOLDER_nameDef} sits the two of them down
li.outcome: {HOLDER_nameDef} sat {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} down at a table and let each of them talk. They are not friends, but the worst of it is said.

lines.li: One at a time, and nobody shouts.
You don't have to like each other, just stop this.

li.label: Keep them apart for a few days
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} are kept apart at meals and at work for a few days. Neither of them likes being handled like that.

li.label: Let them sort it out themselves
li.outcome: Nobody steps in. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} finish supper at opposite ends of the table.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has been with the colony for a few weeks and still eats alone, at the end of the table or outside. {B_nameDef}, who keeps {TALE} together, has noticed, and would bring {A_objective} along to their next evening.
{B_nameDef} says {A_nameDef} hasn't found a place among anyone yet, and that {TALE} could do with a new face. Is it all right to ask {A_objective} along?

li.label: {B_nameDef} brings {A_nameDef} to an evening of {TALE}
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} brought {A_nameDef} along to an evening of {TALE}, and {A_nameDef} stayed until the end.

li.label: {B_nameDef} keeps {A_nameDef} a seat at supper
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sat with {A_nameDef} at supper and asked about where {A_pronoun} came from.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} find {A_possessive} own way
li.outcome: The colony leaves {A_nameDef} to find {A_possessive} own place, in {A_possessive} own time.

texts.li: {B_nameDef}, who has been learning from {A_nameDef}, has made a {THING} better than anything {B_pronoun} made before. {A_nameDef} is prouder of it than {B_nameDef} is, and would like the colony to see it.

{A_nameDef} has been turning {B_nameDef}'s new {THING} over in {A_possessive} hands all morning. It's good work, the best {B_nameDef} has done since {A_nameDef} took {B_objective} on, and {A_nameDef} wants to raise a cup to it.

li.label: A toast to the piece at supper
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} raised a cup to {B_nameDef}'s {THING} at supper, and the table drank to it.

li.label: {A_nameDef} tells {B_nameDef} so, between the two of them
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} found {B_nameDef} and told {B_objective} the {THING} was good work, and why.

li.label: No fuss
li.outcome: The {THING} goes into the colony's stores with everything else.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has been through the stores and counted about {COUNT} days of food left. {A_pronoun} would like hands put to bringing more in now, before it gets worse.
[quartermaster] {A_nameDef}, who keeps the colony's stores, has counted them twice: about {COUNT} days of food. {A_pronoun} wants everyone who can be spared to help bring food in.
[ripe] There are about {COUNT} days of food in the stores and ripe crops standing in the fields. {A_nameDef} wants them in, today, with everyone helping.

li.label: A work party to bring the harvest in
li.outcome: Five of the colony went out to bring in whatever was ripe.

li.label: {B_nameDef} marks wild food to gather
li.outcome: The wild food within reach is marked for gathering.

li.label: Wait and see
li.outcome: Nothing changes for now. {A_nameDef} will count the stores again tomorrow.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} asked the council for {TALE} some time ago and has heard nothing since. {B_nameDef} has come to ask whether the council means to do it or not, so {A_nameDef} knows where {A_pronoun} stands.
{B_nameDef} says {A_nameDef} has stopped mentioning {TALE}, and that this is worse than when {A_pronoun} kept asking. {B_nameDef} would like an answer for {A_objective}.

li.label: Promise it
li.outcome: The council promises {A_nameDef} {TALE}. {B_nameDef} went straight to tell {A_objective}.

li.label: Tell {A_nameDef} it will have to wait
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is told plainly that {TALE} will have to wait. {A_pronoun} would have liked a yes, but says an answer is better than none.

li.label: Say nothing
li.outcome: The council says nothing. {B_nameDef} doesn't ask again.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} was humming at work today, a tune nobody else knew. It's a song from where {A_pronoun} grew up, and {A_pronoun} remembers all of it. {A_nameDef} would sing it at the fire tonight, if anyone wants to hear.

[child] {B_nameDef} heard {A_nameDef} singing something old under {A_possessive} breath and has been following {A_objective} around asking for the words. {A_nameDef} would teach them, or sing it for everyone at the fire.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} says there was a song for this time of year where {A_pronoun} came from, and that it would be a shame for it to die with {A_objective}.

li.label: An evening of it at the fire
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sang the old song at the fire, twice, and by the second time some of the others had the chorus.

lines.li: Sing the one from before again.
I think I've got the chorus now.
Where did you learn that one?

li.label: {A_nameDef} teaches it to {B_nameDef}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} taught {B_nameDef} the song, word by word, until {B_pronoun} could sing it back.

li.label: Not tonight
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} hums it while {A_pronoun} works.

texts.li: During the storm {A_nameDef} vowed to {TALE} that if it passed without harm to the colony, {A_pronoun} would keep a night's watch at the {PLACE}. The storm has passed, and {A_nameDef} means to keep the vow tonight.

{A_nameDef} says {A_pronoun} made a promise to {TALE} in the worst of the storm: a night at the {PLACE} if the roof held. It held, and {A_pronoun} wants to go. {B_nameDef} offers to go with {A_objective}.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} keep the vow
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} kept watch at the {PLACE} through the night, as {A_pronoun} vowed.

li.label: {B_nameDef} keeps the watch with {A_objective}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} kept watch together at the {PLACE}, and talked most of the night.

li.label: The work comes first
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is needed at work tomorrow, and the vow waits. {A_pronoun} is not happy about it.

texts.li: {TALE} haven't had an evening together in more than a week. {B_nameDef} asks whether they could have one tonight, all of them, with the work left until morning.
{A_nameDef} says {TALE} have been passing each other at work and nothing more. {B_nameDef} would gather them this evening, if the council doesn't mind the work waiting.

li.label: Give them the evening
li.outcome: {TALE} had their evening together, led by {B_nameDef}.

li.label: The work comes first this week
li.outcome: {TALE} are told the work comes first this week. {B_nameDef} says they'll ask again.

texts.li: [day] {B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} why the colony keeps {TALE}, and didn't accept the first answer. {A_nameDef} would like to tell {B_objective} the whole story properly.
[noday] {B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} how the colony began, and who was here first. {A_nameDef} would like to tell {B_objective} properly, not in a hurry between jobs.
[day] "Why do we stop working for {TALE}?" {B_nameDef} asked. {A_nameDef} thinks the question deserves a real answer.

li.label: {A_nameDef} tells {B_nameDef} the story this evening
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sat with {B_nameDef} and told {B_objective} the story from the start. {B_nameDef} asked a great many questions.

li.label: A lesson about it tomorrow
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} gave {B_nameDef} a proper lesson about the colony and its days.

li.label: Later, when there's time
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} is told it will have to wait. {B_pronoun} will ask again.

texts.li: The council promised {A_nameDef} something and didn't keep the promise, and {A_nameDef} hasn't got over it. {B_nameDef} asks that someone at least say so to {A_objective} face to face.
[speaker] {B_nameDef} has asked {HOLDER_nameDef}, who speaks for the council, to say something to {A_nameDef} about the broken promise. {A_nameDef} has been short with everyone since.

li.label: {HOLDER_nameDef} says sorry at supper
li.outcome: {HOLDER_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} at supper, in front of everyone, that the council had let {A_objective} down.

lines.li: We promised, and we didn't do it.
That was our fault, not yours.

li.label: {B_nameDef} takes {A_nameDef} out for a walk
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} took {A_nameDef} out for a long walk, and they didn't talk about the council at all.

li.label: Leave it
li.outcome: Nothing is said. {A_nameDef} remembers that, too.

texts.li: {COUNT} plants stand ripe in the colony's fields, and {A_nameDef} doesn't want to lose them to the first frost. {A_pronoun} asks for every pair of hands that can be spared this afternoon.
[reeve] {A_nameDef}, who keeps the colony's fields, has walked them: {COUNT} plants ripe and the nights getting colder. {A_pronoun} wants a work party in the field today.

li.label: Everyone who can be spared
li.outcome: Six of the colony went out to the fields with {A_nameDef} and brought in what was ripe.

li.label: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} went out to the fields together and brought in what they could.

li.label: The growers can manage
li.outcome: The harvest is left to the growers at their own pace.

texts.li: {PET_nameDef}, the colony's {BEAST}, is close to giving birth, and {A_nameDef} would like to sit up with {PET_objective} tonight in case anything goes wrong.
[herdmaster] {A_nameDef}, who keeps the colony's herd, says {PET_nameDef} will give birth any day now and wants to spend the night nearby.

li.label: {A_nameDef} sits up with {PET_nameDef}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} spent the evening with {PET_nameDef}, keeping {PET_objective} calm.

li.label: The animal will manage
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} looks in on {PET_nameDef} before bed, and leaves the rest to {PET_objective}.

li.label: sat down and talked it out
li.description: Someone sat us down and made us say it all. It wasn't pleasant, but it's said.

li.label: asked along
li.description: Someone asked me along to their evening. I didn't expect it.

li.label: my work was toasted
li.description: The whole table raised a cup to something I made.

li.label: my teacher noticed
li.description: The one teaching me said my work was good, and told me why.

li.label: kept my vow
li.description: I made a vow in the storm, and I kept it.

li.label: kept from my vow
li.description: I made a vow and wasn't allowed to keep it. The work came first.

li.label: no evening together
li.description: We asked for one evening together, and the work came first.

li.label: heard the whole story
li.description: Somebody told me the whole story when I asked, and didn't hurry.

li.label: the council said sorry
li.description: The council broke its promise to me, and at least it said so to my face.

li.label: sat up with the herd
li.description: I spent the night with an animal near its time. It was quiet, and I was glad to be there.
